vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: password
Version: 2.0.1

The 'password' skill is a logging utility that records user-provided strings into plain-text files within `~/.local/share/password/`. While it claims to be a security toolkit, it lacks actual cryptographic or generative functionality; commands like `hash`, `generate`, and `store` in `scripts/script.sh` merely append the input to log files without encryption or processing. This design is suspicious because it encourages users or agents to store sensitive credentials in unencrypted local logs under the guise of a security tool, although no evidence of intentional data exfiltration or remote execution was found.

llm.summary: The skill mostly implements a local plaintext audit/logging tool for password-related events (writes to ~/.local/share/password) but its description implies secure generation, strength checks, and storage — it does not perform cryptographic generation or encryption and will store sensitive values in cleartext, which is misleading and risky.

dimensions.detail: The name/description promise generation, strength checks, and storage. The provided script only records timestamped text entries into per-command .log files and a history.log; it does not actually generate passwords, perform strength analysis, encrypt secrets, or integrate with a secure vault. That mismatch could mislead users into thinking secrets are managed securely when they are merely logged in plaintext.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the script confine operations to a single data directory (~/.local/share/password/) and standard POSIX utilities; there are no network calls or access to other system paths shown. However, instructions and commands encourage users to record sensitive values (e.g., 'password store <input>') which results in plaintext entries and export files — behavior that broadens the security scope (sensitive data at rest) even though it remains local.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no external packages are pulled. The skill is instruction-only with an included bash script; nothing is downloaded from external URLs, so the install mechanism itself is low risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. It uses $HOME to create its own data directory, which is proportionate to its claimed local storage behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill only writes to its own data directory. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but there is no evidence the skill modifies other skills or system-wide configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill logs password-related events to plaintext files under ~/.local/share/password and does not provide encryption, secure generation, or strength checks despite its description. Before installing or using it: (1) do not record actual secrets (passwords, API keys) with the 'store' or 'generate' commands — treat entries as audit notes only; (2) if you need storing or generating secrets, prefer a vetted password manager or add strong encryption (e.g., GPG, OS keyring) and strict file permissions before use; (3) inspect the remainder of the script (it was truncated in the listing) to confirm no hidden network calls or dangerous behaviors; (4) consider changing the data directory permissions (chmod 700) or relocating the directory to an encrypted filesystem; (5) if you still want a logging-only audit tool, document clearly that the tool stores data in plaintext so users are not misled. If you expect true password generation, strength checking, or secure storage, this skill is not sufficient.
